geeklist.title: '24 Dice Tower West Virtual Flea Market
geeklist.description:
[center][b]DTW kicks off March 6th, but why wait to spend money until then? On the flip side, maybe you'll sell a few items ahead of time so you can buy more stuff when you get there![/b]
[IMG]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/41d157_53fc1511dcec4a6b98175ae3a6eb0e37~mv2_d_1372_1474_s_2.gif[/IMG][/center]
[b]What's this list for?[/b]
If you have items you'd like to sell at Dice Tower West, you can list them here. This is not part of the physical flea market that is happening at the con. This is just a forum to work out deals in advance of the con, so you can pack/plan accordingly.
[b]***Scheduled meet-up Friday 10 AM.***[/b]
Not everyone will be able to make this. It's recommended that you exchange contact info and touch base with your trade partner(s) before the con.
********************************************************************************
[b]Guidelines[/b]
When you list your item, include the condition of the game and the price you'd like to sell it for. It's up to you to decide how you want the item to be sold (e.g. Fixed price, auction, best offer, etc). The transaction will be handled by you from beginning to end. Don't get offended by offers below your asking price. This is a format where haggling is accepted, if not expected.
Please be aware, not everyone attends the entire convention. If this is you, it's helpful to list when you will/won't be there to avoid missing your buyer/seller.
[b]Don't be a jerk![/b] By agreeing to buy/sell a game, your partner is counting on you to keep your word. They are losing the chance to buy/sell with another person. Please only agree if you plan on honoring your word. If life happens and you won't be able to complete your transaction, please send them a direct message asap. Also, there is no need to publicly questions prices. The market will dictate the value, it's not up to you to police it:cool:
It's best not to delete sold listings. This is your proof of the agreed price and condition. Just mark them as "sold" or change the photo to one that says "sold". You can change the picture id to 6602898 & it will display this :arrowS:.
[ImageID=6602898 micro]
Be careful of double-listing 1 game. If you plan on listing a game here and in the math trade, make sure you don't commit it to 2 people. Remove it from the math trade as soon as you have a deal here, or hold off on listing it until after the trade.
Please do not delete and repost your game or post it to this list more than once in an effort to "bump" to the front of the line.
********************************************************************************
Most transactions will be handled at the con (ie: exchange cash for the game). You are expected to process your transactions in the Marketplace to pay BGG their 3% commission on all sales assisted by this site. The 3% is automatically added to Geek Marketplace transactions.
There are a couple of ways you can capture the items you have sold on the list:
1. List each transaction in the marketplace. There is a quick link to do this under each of your listings. Then, send your buyer the link for the listing.
2. You can also create a marketplace dummy sale item something like "Miscellaneous - DTW43 VFM Commission" as the item type/description and price it at whatever ends up being your total for sales, then "buy" it yourself. This will generate a seller's invoice via Geek Mail for the 3% commission payable by PayPal.
3. BGG's commission is on the honor system and will not be policed by me.
******************************************************************************** Amazing tools provided by [user=Carnage994][/user]
Alpha List of Games Offered: [url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/328677][/url] Quick add tool: [url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/328677][/url]
You can post games you want to buy here: [geeklist=328679][/geeklist]

Ben, are there plans to enforce an occupancy limit for the trade/sell rooms this year? Particularly the Sunday market, I don't think the math trade/flea market exchange meetup was really an issue.
I think the bigger issue is the way it's arranged. The aisles really need to be wider or a one way direction needs to be enforced. Preferably the wider aisles....
I agree, but more space between people who purchased space would help out a lot. Also, removing the island of tables.

I thought the virtual flea market was fine, it was the actual physical flea market that was the real issue.
Because they opened both doors at the same time with a U-Shaped layout, everyone got stuck in the middle.
Hoping it's one-way traffic this year!
They need a bigger space for the physical flea market, period. It’s always a zoo.

I also wanna point out last year for the physical market that they didn't use the whole room. The single lane wasn't wide enough, if the outer sellers were closer to the wall (they had PLENTY of space behind them for some reason) it wouldn't have ended up the disaster that it was.

Also maybe don't use seller tables to enforce an actual U shape. If you just have two straight lanes, when people reach the end of one lane, they have all the space to walk around others when moving over to the next lane. Or even take a breather if one feels it is too crowded.
And if anyone is afraid there might be a "security" issue with people going behind sellers and taking their stuff when reaching the end of a lane, block entry behind the sellers with a table but otherwise leave the end of lane space wide open for people to freely move.
I'm going strictly table this year and have to imagine there will be adjustments after last year.

This will be my third year going and I'm also pretty familiar with Vegas. A lot of your questions can be asked in the DTW scheduler system under Lobbies and General Chat. People are starting to use the scheduler more now that we're just over a month away, so you should have quick answers to your questions. But, I'll answer the above questions here to the best of my ability.
1) The walk to the Strip from the Rio isn't the safest, but it's not terrible. You'll be walking on the freeway overpass (there's plenty of sidewalk. The issue is trying to cross the street on the other side of the freeway. It's lighted but it IS an onramp to the freeway, so you have to be really careful and quick sometimes.). It's about a 5-10 minute walk, not far. 2) Not sure if you are looking for full service restaurants or fast food. There's a Subway and TGIFridays across the street in the Gold Coast casino. Across the street diagonally from the Rio is a Chick-Fil-A, Denny's, and Del Taco. The Rio has a Smashburger, Hash House A GoGo (full service), and American Diner (full service as well, but overpriced in my opinion.). All casinos will also have their own steakhouse as well, but I have only eaten at one: Gallagher's at New York New York. Down the street from the Rio going away from the strip is Blueberry Hill. This is a restaurant similar to a Denny's or IHOP, but better. Good food and good prices, but it can be very busy (which is a good sign. Locals love this place.) I like walking to the Strip and heading to the Flamingo and Harrah's area. They have a pizza place inside Harrah's that's pretty good. Outside the Flamingo is a Gordon Ramsey Fish & Chips which is also quick and very good as well as an In-N-Out. Flamingo has a Margaritaville. I'm not much of a foodie as I'm pretty much the opposite, so I stick with comfort foods and such, so maybe others can give other suggestions as well. 3) If by Major Events you mean tournaments and competitions, you'll have to check the Scheduler on Cardboard Events. They're listed there and you sign up in there. There is no Texas Hold'em played at DTW. It's held in a casino, so you'd have to go to the casino's poker room to play Hold'em. DTW doesn't really run any tournaments or contests of their own as the ones that are held there, are part of the World Series of Board Gaming qualifiers. It DOES appear there is a Dune tournament though. Other than that, last year Tom ran a large multi-table game of Ready, Set, Bet and the usual Marble Races. The previous year instead of Ready, Set, Bet, it was Wits & Wagers. So, it should be either of those this year, but leaning toward Ready, Set, Bet as he didn't get to participate last year having suffered laryngitis. 4) Hot Games Room is ALWAYS packed. It's not a large room and there's barely enough space between tables to walk around. It's also very loud and can get hot in there. There are also a few of the hot games set up in the main hall as well near the stage. Just make a few passes through the room to see where players are at and if they're near the end of their game and if so, post by the wall and wait for them to finish scoring and resetting the game. It is customary in the Hot Games Room to reset the game for the next group when you are done. Play to Win can also be iffy. Last year, there were barely any games for the times I was looking and then suddenly, the last day or two it was packed. Just keep checking in and seeing what's available or if you see someone about to play one of them, jump in with them. Everyone who plays gets scanned in for a chance to win it, not just the person to grab it. They usually have around 50-100 games on the Play to Win shelf. 5) Nearest store is across the street next to the Chick-Fil-A. It's a Walgreens or a CVS, but I'm 98% sure it's Walgreens. If you need to get any cash out, use their ATM. It's only $3 fee instead of the $8-10 fee in the casinos. 6) Check-in/check-out process is very easy. Every game has a QR code on the box and the badge you will receive has one as well. They'll scan your badge and the game and you're good to go. Check-in, just hand it in to the clerk and they'll take care of it. That's it. 7) There are three shows at the Rio: Penn & Teller magic show, WOW cirque du soleil style show, and Chippendales. Outside of that: There's Piff the Magic Dragon at Flamingo, and Potted Potter at Bally's which is fun if you're a Harry Potter fan or going with Potter fans. Outside of that, you'll have to check online to see what's showing and where. There's also good prices for shows if you buy them in Vegas. Look for the red booths along the strip called Tix4Vegas. They are tickets for the same day and are discounted as a way to help sell out the shows.

Thomas is mostly right with a few corrections:
There is a new food hall that opened this month and a few more food options this year. There is also Pho, Dim Sum, and we're a short Lyft away from Vegas' China Town area. https://www.riolasvegas.com/food-and-drink
I'd say the Strip is 10-15 away by foot, It's not bad but do not plan on a 5 minute walk. It will take you 5 minutes to get from your room out to the street and another 10 to get to the closest point on the strip.
There are tournaments, look for the banner in the main hall. There are major events like a top 10, Marble Run, Q&As, etc, just look for a schedule in your program.

Correct me if I am misremembering from last year's DTW VFM exchange, but I believe that everyone randomly grabbed a table and it was difficult to find a lot of people without more standardization. Any chance that we can do an alphabet system by username this time? It works really well for both the EsCon VFM in San Diego and the Strategicon VFM in Los Angeles. In case it's an option, here's the cut/paste from the EsCon VFM header about it: "General Guidelines Day of Exchange -- The outside area will have letters on the ground [/table/wall] (e.g. "A", "B", "C", etc.) -- Sellers: Upon arriving promptly at [___], please post yourself at the station that corresponds to the first letter of YOUR username. -- Buyers: Pay seller prior to arriving or bring cash in envelope to the seller's username letter (posted on the ground [/table/wall] at meet-up location. -- If you are buying AND selling, consider bringing a friend to collect your purchased games while you are positioned at your station to exchange your sold games. -- If you have no friends/children/servants, please alert your sellers of your situation and maybe they will come to you to make the exchange."
I was just going to yell out my buyers usernames and hope someone showed up

Below is the area where we will meet up on Friday morning at 10, in the open gaming area, not to be confused with the main hall where the vendors will be set up.
[imageid=8071255 large]
As others have mentioned, the buddy system works best if you have a large amount of transactions. 1 person to stay with your pile and distribute them, and another to act as a rover.
Be on time, or communicate if you won't. It seems like all the deals are done within the first 15 minutes, then 25 people have to stay for another half hour looking for the 1 person who's either running late or isn't coming and didn't communicate. Don't be that 1 person.
Having a sign with your name/avatar works well. Remember you are your username, and even if that's not what your momma calls you, it's the only way we know you🤣 Print a list of everyone you're looking for. If Wifi is spotty, it sucks to run around looking for signal when your list is only online.
Have change. You can use the casino ATM's to break bills for free, but it's expensive to withdraw money. Some folks like to have envelopes with the exact amount ready to go, this works really well.
I 100% agree with the envelope thing. It's soooo much faster and cleaner to hand an envelope. But I also post it note the buyer and price on everything I sell.

Thanks to everyone for easy exchanges this year! Thanks to Ben and his volunteer group for organizing and improving every year!

Thank you all for the love and for making this year's flea market VFM, FM, & MT amazing. I started running these because I wanted more deals for myself, and to find such a large group of people that love "the deal" as much as the games themselves, makes me feel at home.
A HUGE shout-out to the amazing group of folks who helped set up and tear down the room for the flea market. It was the only difference between this year's success and last year's failure. I literally could not have done it without you!
Some notes for next year, as far as I have any control over it:
1) I [b]will[/b] make a separate list for promos.
2) I [b]do not[/b] intend to structure the exchange the way that other cons do. I know some of you wish there were assigned tables and a map. This requires advanced ticketing and potentially limiting the amount of sellers that can join the VFM. I will not do the latter. You have my full blessing to arrange alternate exchanges with your buyers and sellers so you don't have to attend. Or, you can vitriolically complain about it without realizing I was the person standing next to you 😂😂😂.
I hope you all had a fun and safe time in Vegas. See you all in 2025!
Feels like this is about to start up again… ‘Tis that time of year! 🙂 🙂

item.comment: I’ve never bought from the flea market but I’d like to purchase this. I’ll be at DTW the first day to Saturday.

The virtual flea market is held on Friday morning at 10:00 (I get there about 9:45 to find a space to set up). They have done this in the past so it is pretty well organized and runs smoothly. In the past it has been in the main hall with the demo games and dealers in one corner of the room. Best part is that there is no line to get in unlike the regular flea market so much quicker to get what you want and get out. Most people have a sign with their ID so relatively easy to find folks you are looking for. I can only take cash as I am an old guy without the new fangled money transfer technology. If you are still interested please let me know.
If its still available, I will buy it for $20, thanks.
I have not heard anything for 3 weeks now so I assume not interested. Sold to you for $20

Wow, just wow
[q="andresfresquez"]Let me give [user=steveusa] a chance to match your $20, otherwise, its yours, sorry. Ultimately, I decide how the game is sold and this seems fair to me. [/q]

Let me quote the Guidlines: "
Guidelines
When you list your item, include the condition of the game and the price you'd like to sell it for. It's up to you to decide how you want the item to be sold (e.g. Fixed price, auction, best offer, etc). The transaction will be handled by you from beginning to end. Don't get offended by offers below your asking price. This is a format where haggling is accepted, if not expected."
[i]Now[/i] you're quiet [user=itzbharath] Don't be so quick to send judgmental comments. We might play a game together someday.
to [user=vnemecek] Read the guidelines. It's not about what [i]you[/i] think is fair. Make your own flea market next time. I don't mind being wrong, I just want to get rid of games

Please keep things civil, everyone. This happens every year and isn't even the 1st listing where someone "bid" over the asking price in this year's market. Andres did the noble thing and sold it to the 1st person to meet the asking price, even though that meant leaving some money on the table.
It was an issue between the seller and 2 buyers, the additional opinions did not solve anything.
As a personal note, "or best offer" is usually interpreted as a willingness to accept less, but would have eliminated this situation, so maybe some of you will want to add that in the future. Also, if I missed out on a game I wanted because someone beat me to it, I will sometimes offer a "backup offer" if it falls through, but I don't bid for over the asking price, as to not put the seller in this situation.
I don't think there was an ounce of malice in this entire situation, just gamers excited about games. 4 weeks from Wednesday!!!

item.comment: Can you say more about the condition of this one — i.e., what makes it “very good” rather than like new?

Yeah, I say "Very Good" because the game has been opened and played, but there are no missing components or signs of wear and tear on anything. You can expect that most of the cardboard chits to be punched, packs of cards to be opened and shuffled, and all of the components to be sorted and packed as I saw fit.
For my copy of Iwari, I just checked, and it has all of the components nicely fitted in a great insert that came with the box. It does have an original token sheet with half of the tokens still in it, and it looks like there is an unopened pack of cards likely for an expansion. Even the exterior of the box doesn't have any signs of wear that I would generally consider negligible, so overall this might be legitimately "Like New", I just always err on the side of caution describing my games because some people might believe "Like New" to be indistinguishible from a new product.

Thanks for the detailed description! I’ll bid $55.
Just one other question: does this copy include the three paid metal add-ons: the Storm mini-expansion, the totem score tracker, and the territory scoring markers?
It does not have the Storm mini-expansion or Metal Totem, but it does include the metal scoring markers with the cotton bag to store them.

[-]Dark Tower ‐ English edition (1981) Publisher: Milton Bradley
Complete (missing one of 42 red pegs but only 40 are used in the game). Also includes two spare bulbs and plastic tubes used for pulling the old bulbs. Condition generally good to VG, especially considering its age. The tower works and includes two fresh alkaline D cells installed. Note: sometimes the tower doesn't want to start; in this case, if you pick up the tower, invert it and then do the self-test startup, it will start and then the tower can be put back upright and it will play normally. The board is a bit warped, the back shows wear and the corners that go into the plastic clips is warn, making it hard to attach them. The box is in poor condition with tears and tape.

Hi Christina,
Thank you! I love organizing, it's half the joy of the hobby for me. The AH binder was a Christmas present from my wife. We're happy to have it go to another home who will enjoy it, though! (She hates creatures or horror themes, so this is just sitting on the shelf.)
I would be interested in the Return to Night of the Zealot and Return to Dunwich Legacy if you were open to selling them separate.

Hi,
Unfortunately, I have character cards from Dunwich in the folders and Return to Night mixed in with the core Night. Honestly, looking at prices of Return to Night of the Zealot, I'd say you may want to think of buying it all, too :)

This is for a lot of 4 titles from the Mystery Experiences Company. These were only available through a subscription service, and each box contains one puzzle. Solving the puzzles sometimes require information from the now-defunct website. Some people have had success using the archived site or resources uploaded on the Facebook page, but it was too bothersome for our liking - but this may be for you if you want the added challenge! Titles are: The Lost City I Am The Raven Tombs of the Pharoah Jack the Ripper

item.comment: I really like one called Hand and Foot, it's a melding race game trying to be the first team to "go out" with higher and higher requirements each round to even be allowed to start playing cards.
I've only recently heard of Hand and Foot, but have never played it. Is it more regional? Never heard of it while growing up on the East Coast.
I think it is a Michigan/midwest thing? Though I learned it from a group of Vegas residents/transplants.

My Mom got me into Pinochle, and it is really good. Of course, Spades is amazing. As far as more "gamer-y" partnership games, one that I want to play more of at 4p (you play individually at 3p) is [thing=383459][/thing]. But yeah, Tichu is my favorite card game. I got the guy who introduced me to it to go down the "foreign deck" rabbit hole so now he has like 5 decks ordered from South Korea.
Yes, so many beautiful Tichu decks. My favorite is the Italian deck, which I own. Aurum is on my want-to-try list.

I had a Tichu deck for a little while but never tabled it. I strangely find it hard to table card games, standard deck or something like this.
I love them but the gamers I know are all into medium/heavy board games.
When I visit folks in Vegas is the only time I can play trick takers or partner games.
What's the condition of the deck(s)?
Good condition. Box has a bit of shelf wear since it’s an older edition.
[q="MarkEJohnson"]I’ll take it for $10[/q] Perfect, all yours, and will be great to see you again, Mark. 😊

[-]Space Hulk (Second Edition) ‐ English edition (1996) Publisher: Games Workshop Ltd.
Verified complete. Condition generally VG with a few caveats: the miniatures are undecorated; the decal sheets are there but with their age, they may not be usable; one sergeant's banner poll is broken off (the banner sticker sheets are unused). Many of the genestealers' arms are detached and need to be glued on. Contents are bagged/banded and the miniatures are stored in egg cartons.
The box is in poor condition with water damage (no signs of mold) and much wear.

item.comment: Its hard to find excellent 5 player games but this is one of them. The auction/bidding/bribery mechanism in this game is brilliant and has really stood the test of time. The subtle decision space of when and where to expand your plot and predict water movement creates for deep, rich, tense and satisfying gameplay. Polish Reprint is nice but this game deserves a a graphic update.

[i][u]THIS[/u] is the perfect game to play with your friends at a convention.[/i] Great variety and “[i]gotcha[/i]” moments lead to lots of laughter and joking around. Edition pictured. Good to very good condition.
As a [i]background game[/i] for a day, weekend, or a longer trip, it walk the perfect line between weird and straightforward, unique and familiar. You get 5 cards so you always get a perfect mix of some that requires deception and some that requires creativity, some that are easy and some that are really challenging. Some rely on things like muscle memory, quick actions, and seizing the right opportunity, while others actually require longer, sneakier planning!!

Your turn looks like this: Flip a tile and then use 10 action points: (Each action costs a different number of points) Move your explorer/Set up a Base Camp/Add a temple/Unearth a treasure/ Recruit more explorers)
Simple. elegent, tactical, deep, fun and plays fast. Absolute gem from the Maestro Wolfgang Kramer.
